chunks: Muhammad ibn Hammam narrated to us in his house in Baghdad in the month of Ramadan in the year 327 AH. He said: Ahmad ibn Mabindath narrated to me in the year 287 AH. He said: Ahmad ibn Hilal narrated to us. He said: al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fadhl narrated to us. He said: Sufyan ibn Ibrahim al-Jariri narrated to us, from his father, from Abu Sadiq, from Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) that he said:

The rule of the Banu al-Abbas is ease, with no hardship in it. If the Turks, the Daylams, the Sindese, the Indians, the Berbers, and the Taylasanese were to unite against them, they would not remove them. They will remain in prosperity of their rule until their followers and companions of their state deviate from them, and Allah will empower a severe man who will emerge from where their rule began. He will not pass by a city but will conquer it, and no banner will be raised against him but he will defeat it, and no blessing will remain but he will remove it. Woe to whoever opposes him. He will continue thus until he triumphs and delivers his victory to a man from my progeny, who will speak the truth and act upon it.

key_terms.عَلَجٌ: A severe or stern man (often used for a specific conqueror)

ai.seo_question: What are the signs of the Abbasid rule and the coming conqueror according to Imam Ali (AS)?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Nu'mani’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* highlights the Abbasid dynasty's political resilience, attributing it to their 'mawali' (clientele) who sustained their rule until a 'Alj' (non-Arab, often interpreted as the Mongols or Ottomans) emerged to dismantle their power. The narrative culminates in the transfer of authority to a specific figure from the Ahl al-Bayt, linking historical geopolitical shifts to the eschatological preparation for the Mahdi's appearance.

en.abdullah-al-shahin: (4) Muhammad bin Hammam narrated from Ahmad bin Mabindath from Ahmad bin Hilal from al-Hasan bin Ali bin Fadhdhal from Sufyan bin Ibraheem al-Jareeri from his father from Abu Sadiq that Amirul Mo’mineen (as) had said:

“During the rule of the Abbasids there will be ease and wealth. Their state will be so strong that even if the Turks, the Daylams, the Sindese, the Indians, the Berbers and the Taylasanese unite together, they will not shake it. They will still live at ease until their followers and commanders deviate from them and until Allah empowers a severe man, who will rise from the place, in which their rule has been established. He will conquer every town he passes by. He will defeat every army standing against him. He will remove every ease and wealth. Woe will be upon whoever resists him. He will still do so until he triumphs. Then he will deliver his victory to a man from my progeny, who will say the truth and will act according to the truth.”
